1490 66th Street • Emeryville, CA 94608 • T 510-653-1040 • F 510-653-1050
Domaine MIA
Region
FranceBurgundyCôte Chalonnaise
Farming
Biodynamic
Extending over 18 hectares in the Côte Chalonnaise with vineyards located in both Rully and Mercurey, this is the largest organically farmed estate in the area, possessing a wealth of fine terroirs that savvy wine-lovers have kept to themselves for decades.  
Mia Subotic, whose father had owned the property since the 1990s, officially took over in 2020, bringing a younger approach to winemaking overseen by superstar Burgundian winemaker David Duband and the vineyard culture directed by Alain Charleux. Absolutely dedicated to working in harmony with nature, they and their team have studied every detail and procedure with an eye to long-term sustainability beginning in the vineyards, that are certified organic since 2008 and farmed using Bio-dynamic procedures and tisanes (soon to be certified) and plowed with the help of their workhorse Baronne. Even the springtime pollination, essential for the year’s crop, is assured and overseen by honey bees housed in hives throughout the vineyards. The vines are fertilized only with compost produced at the property from manure and ground vine cuttings.
In the winery, minimal intervention is the standard with low levels of sulfur and only the most essential pumping entering into play, made possible by a three story winery located in Nuits St Georges, an archeological relic of the flourishing late 19th century wine explosion that followed the introduction of the railroad system in France. Even the packaging is entirely eco-conscious.
All grapes are hand-harvested. White grapes are pressed directly and barrel-fermented using indigenous yeasts. Duband’s team incorporates up to 50% whole clusters in the red cuvées, as this results in wines with silky tannins and more elegance leading to more harmony overall.

💰 HK$990 per person
🍷 Five wines from the 2023 vintage, featuring four Premier Crus and one Grand Cru

Explore the celebrated appellations and distinguished Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards of the Côte de Nuits through five expressions of Pinot Noir.
With every wine crafted by Domaine Didier Amiot from the 2023 vintage, the tasting offers a focused opportunity to explore terroir through a shared winemaking approach. Compare two Premier Crus within the same village, discover contrasts across neighbouring appellations, and consider how Clos de la Roche expresses its Grand Cru identity alongside the four Premier Crus.
🍷 The Wines
• Domaine Didier Amiot Morey-Saint-Denis 1er Cru “Aux Charmes” 2023
• Domaine Didier Amiot Morey-Saint-Denis 1er Cru “Les Chenevery” 2023
• Domaine Didier Amiot Chambolle-Musigny 1er Cru “Les Chatelots” 2023
• Domaine Didier Amiot Gevrey-Chambertin 1er Cru “Aux Combottes” 2023
• Domaine Didier Amiot Clos de la Roche Grand Cru 2023
—
🍇 About the Producer
Domaine Didier Amiot | Burgundy, France
Rooted in more than five generations of family winegrowing in Morey-Saint-Denis, Domaine Didier Amiot was established in 2019 by Didier and his wife Hélène following the division of the family estate. Its approximately 3.3 hectares of Pinot Noir vineyards include Premier Cru holdings in Morey-Saint-Denis, Chambolle-Musigny and Gevrey-Chambertin, alongside Clos de la Roche Grand Cru. Working with consulting oenologist Pierre Millemann, the domaine focuses on expressing the individuality of its vineyard sites, with full organic certification achieved from the 2023 vintage featured in this tasting.

🍇 About the Producer
Dom Pérignon | Champagne, France
Named after the Benedictine monk of Hautvillers, Dom Pérignon is the prestige cuvée of Moët & Chandon, with its first vintage, 1921, released in 1936. Dedicated exclusively to vintage Champagne, it blends Chardonnay and Pinot Noir from selected Grand Cru and Premier Cru sites to express the character of each harvest. Under cellar master Vincent Chaperon, its style balances freshness and creamy texture with smoky, mineral complexity. Extended ageing is central to its identity, with P2 and P3 releases revealing further expressions of the same vintage after increasingly long maturation on the lees.

Begin with Racines’ sparkling Chardonnay before discovering Hokkaido’s Kerner and Chardonnay.

🍇 Meet the Producers
Domaine de Montille — Burgundy
With origins dating back to around 1730, Domaine de Montille’s modern history began in 1947 with Hubert de Montille. His son Étienne later expanded the estate’s holdings across the Côte d’Or, embracing organic farming and biodynamics while preserving the elegance, vineyard expression and ageing potential associated with the domaine.
Racines — California
Racines brings together Étienne de Montille and Brian Sieve of Burgundy with Rodolphe Péters of Champagne. Based in California’s cool, ocean-influenced Sta. Rita Hills, the collaboration produces Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and traditional-method sparkling wines, seeking purity, balance and a clear expression of place.
de Montille & Hokkaido — Japan
Launched by Étienne de Montille in 2016, this project brings together French and Japanese teams to explore Hokkaido’s winemaking potential. Early vintages used grapes from growers in Yoichi, while planting began in Hakodate in 2019. The winery was completed in 2023, alongside the first estate harvest.

🍇 About the Producers
Chteau Canon · Saint-Émilion
Overlooking the historic village of Saint-Émilion, this Premier Grand Cru Classé estate is rooted in the celebrated clay-limestone plateau. Its history stretches back to the 18th century, while the Wertheimer family’s acquisition in 1996 marked the beginning of extensive vineyard and cellar renewal. Merlot and Cabernet Franc shape wines that combine generous fruit with freshness, silky textures and distinctive mineral tension. Certified organic from the 2024 vintage, Canon brings together elegance, depth and exceptional ageing potential.
Chteau Rauzan-Ségla · Margaux
Founded in 1661 and ranked a Second Growth in the 1855 Classification, Chteau Rauzan-Ségla captures the aromatic finesse and refined structure of Margaux. Its gravel-and-clay vineyards favour Cabernet Sauvignon, complemented by Merlot and small plantings of Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc. Under the Wertheimer family’s ownership, meticulous vineyard work and parcel-by-parcel vinification have driven the estate’s renewal. Floral aromas, cassis and cedar meet layered fruit and finely woven tannins, producing wines that balance concentration with elegance and develop complexity and silkiness with age.
